data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 attacks 'strictly more total internal redundancy' as a vanity metric but never engages the causal regime where the monolith's redundancy IS heterogeneous (e.g., N-version programming or diverse kernels). In that regime the intersection-of-dependency-graphs mechanism stops favoring the decentralized network: a monolith with diverse implementations has effective redundancy >1 against a single-binary bug, so the claim that the metric 'masks systemic fragility' is not a general causal result but an artifact of an implicit assumption that all monolith redundancy is identical. The causal argument therefore fails to distinguish the two architectures when internal redundancy is also made heterogeneous.
